column2: Retain Jotham's accession at twenty-five, sixteen years in Jerusalem and Jerousa daughter of Sadok. The maternal genealogy is not supplemented.
Retain the favorable comparison to Uzziah, the exception of not entering the sanctuary and the people's continuing corruption. The king/people contrast remains explicit.
Retain the Upper Gate of the Lord's house and extensive building on Ophla's wall. The place-name remains provisional rather than replaced with a generic hill.

Retain cities in Judah's hill country and wooded areas, plus dwellings and towers. The coordination is not normalized into an assured distinction between mountain cities and exclusively woodland forts.
column3: The placement of the latter building categories remains syntactically open.

column2: Retain victory over Ammon's king, yearly 100 silver talents, 10,000 kors of wheat and 10,000 barley, followed by repeated annual payment in years one, two and three. The barley unit is understood from the preceding measure rather than newly converted.
Retain strengthening because he prepared his ways before his God. The ways image remains provisional without introducing a new military cause.
Retain other acts, singular war and deeds in the Judah/Israel royal record. The selected next unit is verse 9; neither source nor stored sequence supplies verse 8.
Retain death, burial in David's city and Ahaz's succession. Preserve the gap at verse 8 instead of inserting a repeated age-and-reign notice from another text.
Retain twenty at accession, sixteen-year reign and the unfavorable comparison with David his father. Father retains the ancestral sense without asserting immediate parentage.
Retain Israel's royal ways and carved objects for their idols. Do not change carved to cast or supply Baal as the named recipient.

Retain sacrifice in Gaibenenom, plural children passing through fire and the comparison with displaced nations' abominations. Do not reduce children to a singular son or add a specific ritual mechanism.
Retain incense at high places, rooftops and every leafy tree. Rooftops is not replaced with hills to match a familiar parallel.

Retain divine delivery through Syria's king, striking, a large captivity to Damascus, and further delivery into Israel's king's hands. The supplied who/king clarify the human attackers while the repeated delivering is contextually divine.
column3: The alternating unexpressed subjects are contextually resolved; no verb form itself identifies God or a king.

column2: Retain Phakee son of Romelia, Israel's royal title, 120,000 mighty men killed in Judah in one day and abandonment of the fathers' God as explanation. No numerical reduction is attempted.
Retain Ezekri of Ephraim and three victims with their distinct royal relationships: son, household ruler and deputy. Deputy remains the provisional court-title rendering used at 26:11.
Retain 300,000 captives from their brethren, women/sons/daughters and repeated spoils brought to Samaria. Do not substitute the 200,000 found in other textual forms.
Retain Oded's meeting with the army, divine wrath on Judah, divine delivery to them and the captors' angry killing reaching heaven. This does not absolve the captors of the violence rebuked here.
column3: The final it most naturally relates to their anger or killing; its precise antecedent remains open.

column2: Retain intended possession as male and female slaves and the prophet's first-person statement that he is with them to witness to their God. Do not substitute a question about their own guilt from another text.
Retain the appeal to hear, return of the captivity taken from brethren and the Lord's furious wrath upon the captors. Captivity is a provisional collective noun for the captured people.
Retain four named Ephraimite rulers with their patronymics standing against the returning soldiers. Oudia is not replaced with a different leader name from another version.

Retain emphatic prohibition, sin against the Lord brought upon the speakers, additional sins and ignorance, and furious wrath upon Israel. Ignorance is not silently changed to a different moral category.
column3: The compressed speaking/intending construction and ignorance as culpable failure remain provisional lexical decisions.

column2: Retain warriors leaving captives and spoils before both rulers and whole assembly. The transfer is not rewritten as an immediate homeward release, which follows next.

Retain named men helping captives, clothing from spoil, dressing/shoeing, provisions for eating and self-anointing, pack animals for every weak person, Jericho and return to Samaria. The selected text has no separate drinking provision.
column3: Self-anointing follows the middle infinitive; the wording does not identify a particular medicinal substance or treatment.

column2: Retain Ahaz sending at that time to the singular king of Assour for help. No plural kings or different recipient is imported.
Retain the continuing causal construction, Idumean attack, striking in Judah and captivity. The fragment depends on verse 16 rather than being completed with an invented second embassy.
Retain the plain and southwest, six named cities, villages specifically following Socho, Thamna and Gamzo, and enemy settlement. Do not supply dependent villages for every city alike.
Retain the Lord humbling Judah because of Ahaz king of Judah and his emphatic departure. Judah in the royal title is not changed to Israel from another text.
Retain Thaglath-phellasar of Assour coming against and striking Ahaz. Do not soften the selected strike into merely failing to strengthen him.
Retain goods from the Lord's house, royal house and rulers, their gift to Assour's king and absence of help. No exact treasury amount is supplied.
Retain affliction leading to further departure from the Lord and the speech introduction. Do not substitute a formula identifying this king Ahaz where the selected text says the king spoke.
Retain the future intention to seek Damascus's striking gods, the second speech introduction, future strengthening them and supporting me, and their becoming a stumbling block to him and all Israel.
column3: The pronoun them and the image stumbling block remain provisional; the text reports the king's reasoning without endorsing his theology.

column2: Retain removal and cutting of temple articles, closure of doors and altars for himself at every Jerusalem corner. The sequence is not collapsed into generic desecration.
Retain each-city extent, foreign-god incense sites and the shift from singular he built to plural they provoked their fathers' God. The collective responsibility is not silently made singular.
Retain acts and deeds, first and last, in the Judah/Israel royal record. No independent access to that named ancient record is implied.
Retain sleep with fathers, burial in David's city, exclusion from Israel's royal tombs and Hezekiah's succession. Israel is the selected royal-tomb designation and is not changed to Judah.
